_rules: Every figure below is read off the vendor's own public page. `source` is that page, `checked` is the day it was read. Nothing here is estimated, and a stale line is a bug — open an issue.

LIST PAY-AS-YOU-GO, always. Where a vendor publishes a per-request rate with no commitment, that is the rate used. Volume discounts, annual commitments and promotional rates are ignored for every vendor, including the maintainer's own.

Where there is no pay-as-you-go rate, the fallback is the cheapest paid plan CONSUMED IN FULL: usd_per_month / (units_per_month / units_per_request) * 1000. That is the most favourable reading for the vendor. A plan you do not exhaust costs more per request than what is shown.

SELF-REPORTED CONSUMPTION WINS. Where the API states what it billed inside its own payload (`usage_path`), the run reads that field per request instead of assuming one unit. Each vendor measures itself; we never meter the vendor.
Free tiers are listed for information and are NEVER used in the cost figures. Every vendor here has one, so comparing on them would rank nothing.

openai/gpt-5.6-luna.note: The judge for the published run. Chosen after measuring five candidates on identical payloads: highest recall of the answer, 1.05M context so no payload can overflow it, and half the price of the next best.

anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5.note: Measured as a candidate judge: perfectly deterministic but the weakest recall of the five tested. Kept here for anyone re-pricing the token column on it.

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.note: List rate. An introductory $2.00/MTok runs until 2026-08-31 and is deliberately not used.

exa-search.note: Docs price text contents at $1/1k pages on top of $7/1k searches, but the API's own costDollars returned $0.007 total on our probes with contents enabled. usage_path makes the run use the vendor's reported figure; the derived rate is the fallback.

firecrawl-search.note: No pay-as-you-go rate published. creditsUsed came back as 2 on every probe, matching the documented search cost.

linkup-standard.note: depth=standard with outputType=searchResults, $0.005/request. sourcedAnswer costs $0.006 and is a synthesis, out of scope here.

parallel-advanced.note: Search API, mode: advanced — more advanced retrieval and compression (about 3 s). $5/1k for 10 results, plus $1/1k for each additional thousand results. Endpoint /v1/search: /v1beta and /alpha also answer but with a different vocabulary of modes, and the Task API field `processor` is silently ignored there.

parallel-basic.note: Search API, mode: basic — quick retrieval, deeper context per call (about 1 s). $5/1k for 10 results, plus $1/1k for each additional thousand results. Endpoint /v1/search: /v1beta and /alpha also answer but with a different vocabulary of modes, and the Task API field `processor` is silently ignored there.

parallel-turbo.note: Search API, mode: turbo — lowest latency and cost (about 200 ms). $1/1k for 10 results, plus $1/1k for each additional thousand results. Endpoint /v1/search: /v1beta and /alpha also answer but with a different vocabulary of modes, and the Task API field `processor` is silently ignored there.

serpdive-krill.note: Costs 0 credits on every plan — it is the free tier, unlimited under fair use. Ranked separately from the paid arms for that reason; see METHOD.md.

serpdive-mako.note: 1 credit at the $0.007 list rate. A launch promotion runs at $0.005 until 2026-10-11 and is deliberately not used.
